abilities.name: Favonius Bladework: Dancing Radiance (Sturm und Drang)
_curatorNotes: The in-stance sibling, authored 2026-09-16 (T0.5). Frames are the base ability's by construction: gcsim's skillAttack()/skillCharge() reuse attackHitmarks/attackFrames/chargeHitmarks/chargeFrames unchanged, so only the element and the multipliers differ (this file's base-normal note 4 already recorded that).

⚠️ N1 IS THE EXCEPTION and is over-claimed by one pill: it has a single hit (attackHitmarks[0] = {19}) and the offset table gives that hit the CONVERSION element, not Anemo — offset is 1 only for N2 and N3, so the pairs run Anemo-first on N2/N3 and conversion-first on N4/N5. Every swing but N1 therefore does carry an Anemo hit. Our one-hit-per-swing model cannot gate a single index of a chain, and one swing in five reads better than five in five reading nothing.

ICD: both halves sit on ICDGroupDefault (the tags differ, not the group), so the Anemo stream is the ordinary 150f / {1,0,0} counter our `normal` and `charged` clocks already model. ⛔ No chargedIcdWindow — the in-stance CA is ICDTagVarkaExtraAttackWind on ICDGroupDefault, not ICDGroupPoleExtraAttack, and he is a claymore user in any case.

⛔ No `P` in input: gcsim has no plunge.go for him and he cannot plunge in Sturm und Drang. gcsim's +5f windup from idle/swap/jump/dash (and +14f for a CA not chained from an attack) is not modeled, as on the base ability.

↻ BOTH CLAYMOERS, 2026-09-16 — this replaces T0.5's "Anemo is the half we take". The Fandom Talent Infobox is explicit where the genshin-db description is a summary: the LEFT hand's DMG "will be converted to Anemo DMG that cannot be overridden by other infusions", and the RIGHT hand deals "corresponding Elemental DMG … following the aforementioned priority order" Pyro > Hydro > Electro > Cryo. `infusion` is the right hand (an ElementRef the party resolves) and `coInfusion` the left.

⚓⚓ THE RIGHT HAND IS THE PRIMARY AND THAT IS LOAD-BEARING TWICE OVER. (1) It decides the ORDER the two are offered in, and measured against the gauge, conversion-then-Anemo at one instant swirls while Anemo-then-conversion produces nothing — so this ordering is what lets Varka SELF-ENABLE his own Swirl, which is what A4 (Azure Fang's Oath), C4 and C6 are all built on. Before this he could only swirl an aura someone else applied. (2) ⚓ Nate 2026-09-16: the infused PHEC hand is what tints the input block, and the block reads `infusion`.

⚠️ NO `fallback` on the right hand, unlike the burst's. gcsim skillAttack (attack.go:115-121) leaves `ele[0]` PHYSICAL when the party has no Pyro/Hydro/Electro/Cryo character and only swaps the ICD tag, so a partyless right hand applies nothing while the left is still Anemo — which is why `coInfusion` fires even when `infusion` resolves to nothing. The BURST does fall back to Anemo (burst.go:31-33), and that asymmetry is gcsim's, not a slip.

⚠️ N1 IS STILL OVER-CLAIMED BY ONE PILL and the reason is unchanged: it is a single hit (attackHitmarks[0] = {19}) carrying the CONVERSION element only, where our one-hit-per-swing model gives every swing both hands. ⚠️ gcsim also alternates which hand leads (offset 1 on N2/N3, so Anemo lands first there and swirls the PREVIOUS swing's aura); at the same frame we get the same swirl COUNT one swing earlier in phase. ⛔ Within-swing ordering is not expressible and is not worth a per-hit element model.

ICD: both halves are ICDGroupDefault on SEPARATE tags (ICDTagVarkaNormalAttackElem / …Wind for the normals, the ExtraAttack pair for the charged attack), which is what the engine's `:co` counter key reproduces. Two clocks started on the same swing stay in phase, so both hands apply on the same 1-in-3 swings — which is what makes the self-swirl land rather than alternate.

⚓ `sC` IS AZURE DEVOUR (KQM's notation — ⚓ Nate 2026-09-16, reading their Varka guide, which writes the two stance specials as `sC` and `sE`). gcsim azureDevourFrames = InitAbilSlice(75), Attack 64, Charge 74, Skill 66, Burst 65, and Dash/Jump/Swap all azureDevourHitmarks[3] = 60. ⚓ FRAMES ONLY: its four hits are `[conv, Anemo, conv, Anemo]` on the same ICDTagVarkaExtraAttack pair the ordinary in-stance charged attack uses, so both claymores come from `infusion`/`coInfusion` and nothing else about it differs from a `C` in this tool. ↻ The cost is modelled since 2026-09-18 — next note.

⚓ THE COST, 2026-09-18 (`specialChargeSpends`, docs/varka-azure-devour-round.md): an `sC` SPENDS a Four Winds' Ascension use. gcsim charge.go skillCharge(): `useSpecialSkill() && Charges(ActionSpecialSkill) > 0` takes skillAzureDevour(), which `SetCD(ActionSpecialSkill, 11*60)` at the attack's START (no delay, unlike Four Winds' own 39f); otherwise the ordinary in-stance charge. Two consequences on the timeline: (1) out of the stance, or with no Pyro/Hydro/Electro/Cryo teammate, `sC` is the ordinary charged attack on `chargeFrames` — the attack it names cannot be performed there (gcsim's `useSpecialSkill()` gate); (2) with no use READY, the token WAITS for one exactly as an `E` on cooldown does (the same charge-queue scan, with the stance's end as the other boundary) — the notation named Azure Devour, and a visible gap is honest where a same-tinted ordinary charge would be a quiet substitution. The spent clock is appended to the END of the queue's chain (charges recharge one at a time), so the next `sE` lands where the queue allows. ⚠️ Nothing is DRAWN for the spend beyond the block: `ActionEvent.spentCharge` records it for a tail or tooltip that is Nate's call.

abilities.name: Windbound Execution
_curatorNotes: FrameMaps re-extracted 2026-07-29 from gcsim main (PR #2668 merged as 5d1ec8c79); post-merge timings replaced the PR-era values.

skill.go: base tap = skillFrames = InitAbilSlice(55) with ActionSwap=49, ActionAttack(N)=49, ActionCharge(C)=49 (omitted, equals swap), ActionSkill(E)=44, ActionBurst(Q)=44, ActionDash(D)=65-19=46, ActionJump(J)=73-30=43. skillHitmark=40, skillCD=16*60 (Press CD 16s).

cooldownStartDelay=39: gcsim main uses a literal SetCDWithDelay(ActionSkill, skillCD, 39) (the PR-era QueueCharTask-wrapped SetCD at the hitmark is gone; the stance AddStatus is still queued at skillHitmark=40).

Four Winds' Ascension variant = specialSkillFrames = InitAbilSlice(68) with ActionAttack(N)=55, ActionCharge(C)=64 (omitted — Azure Devour unmodeled), ActionSkill(E)=56, ActionBurst(Q)=55, ActionDash(D)=75-19=56, ActionJump(J)=85-30=55, ActionWalk=65 (no ActionSwap override → swap=68); fourWindsHitmark=[34,43]; fourWindsCD=11*60. This is the in-stance special skill: it consumes one of 2 charges (11s CD each), deals corresponding-element + Anemo DMG, and only appears when a Pyro/Hydro/Electro/Cryo unit is in the party (skill.go convertToFourWinds). Charge tracking, the 2 uses, and the per-normal-hit -0.5s CD reduction (hexSkillCDReduction) are not modeled. UPDATE 2026-07-17: the parser now honors this variant's conditions (condition-aware variant matching, sQ primitive) — so the base tap-E correctly opens Sturm und Drang again instead of being shadowed by this variant. RESIDUAL: the variant remains a variant of the ONE skill ability, so it shares the base 16s charge queue — a second E only frees up after the 12s stance expires, making Four Winds unreachable in practice. Reaching it faithfully needs a re-author as a separate inStance-gated skill ability with its own CD/charges (Flins Northland Spearstorm pattern).

Hold variant: sidecar Hold CD = 8s. gcsim main (skill.go) does not implement distinct Hold frames — Hold also enters Sturm und Drang, so it inherits the stance behavior/duration and the base skillFrames as an approximation.

durationExtensions: burst.go calls ExtendStatus(skillKey, 2.3*60) — casting Northwind Avatar extends the Sturm und Drang window by 2.3s (gcsim note: 'extends E by 2.3s even though it's not in the description').

Windbound Execution's initial cast deals Anemo AoE DMG (skillInitial, 501.1% ATK at talent L10) and generates 6 Anemo particles (particleCB, 0.3s ICD) — on-field self damage/particles carried by the cast, not authored as team effects.

[A7] Caveat previously stated the in-stance special skill has 2 uses at 11s CD; the 2-use charge count is not separately tracked because the Four Winds' Ascension variant shares the base skill's 16s charge queue (residual already noted in _curatorNotes).

[Hexerei 2026-07-29] Secret Rite (count-gated): gcsim skill.go fourWindsCDRedCB + asc.go hexSkillCDReduction — each in-stance Normal Attack that hits an enemy cuts the Four Winds' Ascension cooldown by 0.5s, raised to 1.0s when Core.Player.GetHexereiCount() >= 2. One reduction per swing, max 15 per stance entry (fourWindsCDStacks, zeroed on stance entry); only skillAttack (in-stance NA) passes the callback — out-of-stance NAs and Charged Attacks do not. Cooldown modification is not expressible in the schema (deferred CD-modification queue), so the factionBonus carries an empty effects array: membership plus the Secret Rite text, no fake model.

[Hexerei 2026-07-29] No permanent (count-independent) patch on Varka: the only IsHexerei site is varka.go:43 (flag defaults on) feeding asc.go hexSkillCDReduction, which still returns 0.5s when the flag is on but fewer than 2 Hexerei are in the party — the whole enhancement is count-gated. No buff / energy / RES-shred / heal piece exists anywhere in the varka package (Hexerei appears at exactly 3 sites: varka.go:43, skill.go:194, asc.go:131-138).

↻ CAVEAT TRIMMED 2026-08-19 (ruthless pass): kept only the on-screen half. Full prior text: "Not modeled: Azure Devour, and the Four Winds' Ascension cooldown reduction from stance Normal Attacks (0.5s per hit, 1s with 2+ Hexerei). Four Winds itself can't be placed — a second E shares the base skill's cooldown, which isn't back up in the stance."

↻ CAVEAT REWRITTEN 2026-09-16 (T0.5): the sentence "Four Winds' Ascension can't be placed" is no longer true — it is a sibling ability with its own 11s clock now (see it below). The remaining two omissions keep their half of the sentence.

↻ CAVEAT REMOVED 2026-09-18: Azure Devour spends its use now (`specialChargeSpends` on the in-stance normal), so the sentence this carried is no longer true and no pixel on this ability is wrong. What is still unmodelled on the kit is C6's free casts (caveated there) and magnitudes (A1's multiplier, C1's Lyrical Libation, C2's strike), none of which draws on this ability.

⚓ A1's MULTIPLIER IS AUTHORED HERE, 2026-09-19 (⚓ Nate), on the house convention Skirk's Return to Oblivion and Neuvillette's A1 use: "deals X% of original DMG" as a +(X − 100) `*DmgBonus` buff. gcsim asc.go a1Multiplier: 1.4 with ≥2 Anemo OR ≥2 of one Pyro/Hydro/Electro/Cryo element in the party, 2.2 with both at once, applied to in-stance Normal/Charged Attacks, Azure Devour and Four Winds' Ascension — so `normalDmgBonus` + `chargeDmgBonus` + `skillDmgBonus` at +40, or +120, under mutually exclusive gates (the +40 rung wraps the +120 condition in `not`). ⚠️ `teamElementCount` is HOLDER-EXCLUDED, so "at least 2 Anemo characters" is `anemo >= 1` here (Varka is the other one). HOSTED ON THIS ABILITY, not on the A1 passive, for the reason Hu Tao's Paramita buff is: an effect on the stance ability fires only on casts OF this ability, where an `onCast skill` on the passive would fire again on every in-stance Four Winds cast and refresh-merge the bar past the stance's end. `duration: 12` is the stance's base length (the Hu Tao / Cyno precedent) — ⚠️ it does not follow the burst's 2.3s extension, so under a `Q` the bar ends 2.3s before the stance does. ⚠️ An ADDITIVE stand-in for a MULTIPLICATIVE bucket, the same approximation the two precedents make: the chip prints +40% / +120% where the game multiplies by 1.4 / 2.2; the three stats share one bar (one window per provenance and duration, the pool round). `skillDmgBonus` reaches only Four Winds in practice — Windbound cannot be recast inside its own stance.
abilities.description:
Manifest the true essence of Favonius Bladework with absolute power. Produces different effects depending on whether the skill is Tapped or Held.

Tap
Leap forward and slash in one fluid motion, dealing AoE Anemo DMG and switching to **Sturm und Drang** mode.
While in Sturm und Drang, Varka's Normal Attack and Charged Attack DMG is increased, and he cannot perform Plunging Attacks. Also, when performing Normal or Charged Attacks, Varka's dual-wielded claymores will deal corresponding Elemental DMG based on the Elemental Types of the characters in the party, respectively. This Elemental DMG cannot be overridden by infusions.
Additionally, when in Sturm und Drang, if there are Pyro, Hydro, Electro or Cryo characters in the party, Varka's Elemental Skill Windbound Execution will be converted to the special Elemental Skill, **Four Winds' Ascension**, dealing corresponding Elemental DMG and Anemo DMG. Additionally, Varka can also expend uses of the special Elemental Skill Four Winds' Ascension to perform a special Charged Attack, Azure Devour, that does not consume stamina to deal corresponding Elemental DMG and Anemo DMG.

Hold
After charging for a while, leap forward. The duration of the charge will increase the distance of the leap.

abilities.name: Four Winds' Ascension
_curatorNotes: ↻ PROMOTED from a skill VARIANT to a state-conditioned SIBLING ability, 2026-09-16 (T0.5) — Odette's Coda shape, which exists for this exact reason: a variant shares the base skill's charge queue, so this 11s cooldown was inert and a second E waited out Windbound Execution's 16s. Measured before: `Xiangling E > Varka E E` placed Four Winds at 16.65s, after the 12s stance had already expired, i.e. it could never be placed at all. resolveActiveAbility prefers a conditioned ability whose condition is definitively TRUE, so with no Pyro/Hydro/Electro/Cryo teammate the teamElementCount half is false and the E falls back to Windbound Execution — which is also gcsim's rule (convertToFourWinds requires conversionElem != Physical).

11s is the official talent table's "Four Winds' Ascension CD" row. ↻ `charges: 2` + `startsOnCooldown` AUTHORED 2026-09-18 (cooldown-reduction round) — the kit's "Starts on cooldown and has 2 maximum uses", which is gcsim's stance-entry block (skill.go:105-118): entering Sturm und Drang SetCDs every ready charge, so the queue is written as one chain (11s, 22s) from the base skill's cooldown clock (`cooldownStartDelay` 39 ≈ the hitmark-40 status add) and re-written on re-entry. The earlier note's reason for NOT authoring `charges` was exactly this block, which `startsOnCooldown` now expresses; the T0.5 fear (a queue starting ready) is gone. ⚠️ Charges recharge ONE AT A TIME (the round's sequential-queue rule), so the second use is 11s behind the first — in a 12s stance (14.3s with the burst extension) the second charge is reachable only through the reduction, which is what the kit intends. C1's "additional use" is a `chargeModifiers` +1.

Frames: specialSkillFrames = InitAbilSlice(68), ActionAttack(N)=55, ActionSkill(E)=56, ActionBurst(Q)=55, ActionDash(D)=75-19=56, ActionJump(J)=85-30=55, no ActionSwap override so swap=68. ActionCharge(C)=64 stays omitted with Azure Devour.

application: the Anemo half only. gcsim skill.go:134-157 fires two hits, fourWindsHitmark = [34, 43], elements [conversionElem, Anemo], both ICDTagNone with Durability 25 — so BOTH apply in game. The conversion element is party-dependent (priority Pyro > Hydro > Electro > Cryo), the same reason the in-stance normal takes only its Anemo half; see that ability's notes.

↻ AUTHORED 2026-09-18 (cooldown-reduction round — docs/cooldown-reduction-round.md §5). The per-hit cooldown reduction IS modelled now (the two `cooldownReduce` effects below); still out: C1's doubled multiplier (magnitude), and Azure Devour's cost.

⚠️⚠️ ORACLE ARTEFACT — `gcsim-frames-diff.md` files this map as DISAGREEING (`N 55→49, E 56→44, Q 55→44, D 56→46, J 55→43, swap 68→49, anim 68→55`) and every one of those "gcsim" numbers is skillFrames, the BASE Windbound Execution's slice. Same for the application row (`+40 anemo`), which is the base skill's hitmark. The dumper casts E and gets the base, because `useSpecialSkill()` needs a Pyro/Hydro/Cryo/Electro teammate and a live Sturm und Drang and the dumper runs ONE character in an empty core. Our values are specialSkillFrames and fourWindsHitmark[1] read straight from skill.go:41-49,134-157. ⛔ DO NOT let `migrate-frames-shape.mjs` resolve these rows "in gcsim's favour" — it would give Four Winds the base skill's frames. Before the promotion the same rows sat harmlessly under "not captured"; they became comparable only because this is an ABILITY now rather than a variant. Same class as the Flins burst and Nilou WS2/WS3 artefacts.

↻ BOTH HITS, 2026-09-16 — this replaces T0.5's Anemo-only entry. gcsim skill.go:134-157 fires `fourWindsHitmark = [34, 43]` with `ele = [conversionElem, Anemo]`, both `ICDTagNone` and Durability 25, and the kit says the same in words: "AoE Elemental DMG … corresponding to the element of the claymore wielded in Varka's right hand, and AoE Anemo DMG". `noICD: true` is that ICDTagNone — ⚓ and it is READ on a cast (run.ts's own comment at the emitReactionsAtCast call names itself as its first reader, and eight characters already rely on it); without it the per-cast counter would swallow the second entry. ⛔ No `fallback` on the right hand: with no PHEC teammate Four Winds is not available at all.

⚓ `sE` is KQM's token for this (⚓ Nate 2026-09-16), the sibling of `sQ` and of `sC` on the normal beside it. ⚠️ BOTH spellings are listed on purpose and `sE` is not merely an alias: in game the stance REPLACES Windbound Execution, so a plain `E` in Sturm und Drang really is Four Winds, and refusing it would be wrong the way Flins's `sQ` is not (his base Q stays castable). The ability a token lands on is still decided by `resolveActiveAbility` from the state and the party, never by the input array — what listing `sE` buys is the eager index's `casts`, so the editor accepts it here and flags it on anyone else.

AUTHORED 2026-09-18 (cooldown-reduction round — docs/cooldown-reduction-round.md §5). Secret Rite: each in-stance Normal Attack that HITS cuts the running Four Winds cooldown by 0.5s, 1.0s with 2+ Hexerei in the party (gcsim skill.go fourWindsCDRedCB + asc.go hexSkillCDReduction), one reduction per swing (`done` flag), at most 15 per stance entry (fourWindsCDStacks, zeroed on entry). Authored as TWO effects under mutually exclusive `teamFaction` gates — the faction-tier rule — each with its own `procCap: 15 per stance`; exact, because a team fact is static for a parse so only one of the pair ever fires. `reduces: "skill"` lands on Four Winds because in the stance the active skill IS Four Winds (gcsim's ReduceActionCooldown override on varka.go:105). ⚠️ Our one-hit-per-swing model matches gcsim's once-per-swing flag; the ~0.5s swing cadence means ~15 hits fill a 12s stance, so the 15 cap binds only with the burst extension. Measured `Xiangling E > Varka E N5 N5 sE`: Four Winds ready at stance + 11s − 5s = 6s.

↻ C1 CORRECTED 2026-09-18 — `chargeModifiers +1` is RETIRED. gcsim keeps the pool at 2 (`SetNumCharges(ActionSpecialSkill, 2)`, never changed) and C1 is `c1OnSkill()` → `ResetActionCooldown(ActionSpecialSkill)`, run right after the stance-entry block has put both charges on cooldown (skill.go:105-118, cons.go:22-28): ONE use handed back at entry, not a third charge starting on cooldown behind the other two. Measured before: `Xiangling E > Varka E sE` at C1 placed Four Winds at 745f, identical to C0, where the game has it castable at entry — a +1 chain [11s, 22s, 33s] can never be reached inside a stance. The reset is authored on the C1 entry as a `cdReset` naming THIS ability (`resetsAbility`), fired by the stance-entering skill under `not inStance` (this ability's own casts are skills too and must not refund themselves) and the PHEC-teammate gate (gcsim's reset sits inside `if convertToFourWinds()`). The extra use is still there: spending the handed-back charge appends an 11s clock after the chain, so C1 reaches three uses per stance (entry, +11s, +22s, each less Secret Rite), which is gcsim's arithmetic exactly.

abilities.name: Northwind Avatar
_curatorNotes: FrameMaps re-extracted 2026-07-29 from gcsim main (PR #2668 merged as 5d1ec8c79); post-merge timings replaced the PR-era values.

burst.go: burstFrames = InitAbilSlice(152) with ActionAttack(N)=137, ActionSkill(E)=138, ActionDash(D)=157-19=138, ActionJump(J)=167-30=137, ActionWalk=140, ActionSwap=136. burstHitmark=[112,131]; SetCD(ActionBurst, 15*60) = 15s CD (no delay); EnergyMax=60. Two Anemo/element slashes (337.0% + 181.4% ATK at talent L10); the first slash converts to the priority Pyro/Hydro/Electro/Cryo element if such a unit is in the party.
gcsim's internal Abil string 'Divine Maiden's Deliverance (Initial)' is a copy-paste placeholder; the real name is Northwind Avatar.

🐛 THE BURST WAS WRONG IN THREE WAYS AT ONCE, all fixed 2026-09-16. gcsim burst.go:30-55 runs `burstHitmark = [112, 131]` over `ele = [conversionElem, Anemo]`, so (1) hit 0 is the RIGHT-HAND element and we authored Anemo — wrong in every party that has a Pyro/Hydro/Electro/Cryo character, i.e. every party this character is built for; (2) both hits are `ICDTagNone` and must apply, where (3) measured, our per-cast standard counter suppressed the second outright — `Varka Q` landed ONE application where the game lands two. ⚓ `fallback: 'anemo'` here and NOWHERE ELSE on this character: the burst is the one site gcsim gives an Anemo fallback (`if ele[0] == defaultConversionElement { ele[0] = Anemo }`), where the normals leave the right hand Physical.
abilities.description:
In the name of the mightiest Knight of Boreas, unleash a powerful double slash attack toward the front, dealing 2 instances of Anemo DMG.
If there are Pyro, Hydro, Electro or Cryo characters in the party, the first slash will be converted to deal corresponding Elemental DMG according to the aforementioned priority order of Elemental Types.

passives.name: Dawn Wind's March
_curatorNotes: gcsim asc.go a1Init/a1UpdateBuff: a1Buff = min(TotalATK*0.1/1000, 0.25) applied to both AnemoP and the conversion element's DmgP; authored as anemoDmgBonus scaling{stat:atk, ratio:1, cap:25}. The matching-element half is omitted (which element depends on party priority Pyro>Hydro>Electro>Cryo).

The a1Multiplier (1.0/1.4/2.2 = deal 100%/140%/220% of original DMG on N/CA/Azure Devour/Four Winds) is a self DMG multiplier with no clean stat mapping and is composition-gated (2 Anemo and/or 2 same PHEC units); flagged, not authored.
This is the Ascension-1 passive (unlocks at Ascension 1).

↻ CAVEAT REMOVED 2026-08-19 (ruthless pass, Nate-approved): no pixel — The authored buff carries `trigger: manual`, and a manual trigger reaches NO planner surface — no bar, no chip, no toggle (167 such effects corpus-wide). So an A1 Varka in a Pyro/Hydro/Electro/Cryo party sees no Anemo DMG Bonus anywhere, where every other always-on stat bonus in the tool chips or bars. The 140%/220% half is trimmed: it is a self DMG multiplier, a magnitude, with no bar shape at all. Category: expected-but-absent.

↻ trigger `manual` → `passive`, 2026-09-16 (T0.5; `docs/manual-trigger-retirement.md` step 3, re-trigger). gcsim asc.go:30-50 adds it as AddStatMod(NewBase(..., -1)) — a PERMANENT conditional stat mod, not a player toggle — so `passive` is the shape it always wanted. `manual` reaches no planner surface at all, which is why an A1 Varka in a Pyro/Hydro/Electro/Cryo party saw no Anemo DMG Bonus anywhere while every other always-on bonus in the tool draws. The teamElementCount gate is unchanged, and the matching-element half stays omitted (the element depends on party priority).

↻ THE CONVERSION-ELEMENT HALF IS AUTHORED 2026-09-16, closing the note above's "the matching-element half is omitted (which element depends on party priority)". gcsim asc.go:26-50 adds the SAME value to AnemoP and to the conversion element's DmgP from one a1Buff, so the four rungs carry the identical `scaling atk ratio 1 cap 25` the Anemo effect does. The priority is the ladder in `conditions`: Pyro on any Pyro teammate, Hydro on none-Pyro-and-a-Hydro, and so on — ⚠️ holder-excluded counts, which is free here because Varka is Anemo.

⚓ A LADDER IN CONDITIONS rather than an `ElementRef`, and the two are not interchangeable: a ref names an ELEMENT and what varies here is the STAT KEY (`pyroDmgBonus` vs `hydroDmgBonus` …), which no element expression reaches. ⚠️ Safe from the §1.H stat-dedupe trap precisely because the four are DIFFERENT stats — ⛔ don't collapse them toward one stat with a conditional value.

↻ THE 140%/220% HALF IS AUTHORED 2026-09-19 — on Windbound Execution (see its last note for why it is hosted there and how the gates are built), replacing the note above's "flagged, not authored". ⚓ Not the first composition-reactive permanent buff: this entry's own stat half and the faction tiers already are; what it needed was only a stat to be said in, and the Skirk/Neuvillette convention supplies it.

passives.name: Wind's Vanguard
_curatorNotes: gcsim asc.go a4Init: swirl (Pyro/Hydro/Electro/Cryo) → a4Stacks up to 4, AddStatus(a4Key, 8*60) refreshes the single shared window; AttackMod adds DmgP = a4Stacks*0.075 to AttackTagNormal, AttackTagExtra, and AdditionalTagVarkaSpecial hits. Modeled as normalDmgBonus + chargeDmgBonus (charged tag = CA and Azure Devour); Four Winds' Ascension (skill tag + special tag) also benefits — noted in caveat. Per-source 1s ICD (a4ICDKey) not modeled.
This is the Ascension-4 passive (unlocks at Ascension 4).

[A7] The per-source 1s ICD (each character can grant at most 1 stack per second) is not enforced: the buff effects carry no procCooldown, so stacks can appear to build faster than the game allows (matches existing _curatorNotes 'Per-source 1s ICD (a4ICDKey) not modeled').

↻ CAVEAT REMOVED 2026-08-19 (ruthless pass, Nate-approved): no pixel — Two buff bars DO draw on a party Swirl — Normal DMG Bonus and Charged DMG Bonus — and both print +7.5%. The effect declares `stacks: {maxStacks: 4}`, which nothing reads: a stackable buff draws as one undifferentiated bar with the per-stack value, so a Varka player who knows the talent gives up to +30% reads 7.5% and wonders why. That is the printed-value pixel. Both existing halves are trimmed away: the specials it 'also boosts' cannot be placed on the timeline in the first place (already caveated on the skill), and the 1s-per-source ICD changes no drawn value because no stack count is rendered. Category: visible-divergence.

↻ Azure Fang's Oath is a STACK RESOURCE now, 2026-09-16 (T0.5), on Neuvillette's Past Draconic Glories idiom: one `gainStacks` key (`azureFangsOath`, max 4, lifetime 8) on the swirl trigger, and the two buffs read it with `perStack`. It replaces `stacks: {maxStacks: 4, durationModel: 'shared'}`, which has NO READER anywhere — so both bars printed a flat +7.5% where the talent gives up to +30%, and the 2026-08-19 pass named exactly that printed value as the pixel.

⚠️ `lifetime` is PER-STACK and gcsim's pool is SHARED-REFRESH (asc.go:100-110: each swirl sets a4Stacks = min(n+1, 4) and re-arms AddStatus(a4Key, 8*60) for the whole pool, resetting to 1 if it had lapsed). We have no shared-duration stack model, so a stack here dies 8s after ITS OWN grant rather than 8s after the last swirl. Consequence: the pool saturates at 4 only while swirls land within ~2.67s of each other, and under-counts by one at slower rates — the safe direction, and still right in the team this character is built for. The alternative, omitting `lifetime`, makes the stacks immortal and over-counts after any gap. ⛔ Don't reach for `drain`: that is a continuous rate, not an expiry.

⚠️ The per-source 1s ICD (a4ICDKey, each character grants at most one stack a second) is still not enforced, and `procCooldown` would be the WRONG tool for it: ours is one clock per effect, so it would cap the pool at one stack per second across the whole party where gcsim caps it per granting character. Pair a gate with the stream we model (the Emilie rule) — ours is one event per reaction, and a global gate would under-count a multi-reactor team.
